                      fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5, fig.align = "center")

We use the tidyverse, so there is nothing new to install.

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
```

Every other chunk of code is switched off with a hash character at the
start of each line. When you reach a chunk, please remove the hashes
(select the lines and press Ctrl+Shift+C, or Cmd+Shift+C on a Mac), run
the chunk, and look at the result before reading on. For the countries
example the code is complete. For your own figure you also replace the
names in capitals with your own file and column names.

Please answer the questions in bold as you reach them. Most of them are
one or two sentences.

## The countries example

`countries` is the 2019 countries file without the four countries
that have no GDP: one row per country, with life expectancy at birth
(`life`, in years) and GDP per person (`gdp`, in current US dollars).

```{r read-countries}
# countries <- read_csv("data/countries_2019.csv") |>
#   filter(!is.na(gdp))
# nrow(countries)
```

This is the figure as a report might draw it: a point for each
country, colored by its WHO region, with GDP on a log scale and the
default text size. It is a reasonable figure for a reader with time to
study it.

```{r report-figure}
# ggplot(countries, aes(x = gdp, y = life, color = region)) +
#   geom_point() +
#   scale_x_log10() +
#   labs(x = "GDP per person (current US dollars, log scale)",
#        y = "Life expectancy at birth (years)",
#        color = "WHO region")
```

`countries_model` is the straight line fitted to life expectancy
against the logarithm of GDP. Its slope is the difference in life
expectancy for a tenfold difference in GDP per person.

```{r countries-model}
# countries_model <- lm(life ~ log10(gdp), data = countries)
# coef(countries_model)
```

`slide_figure` is the same data drawn for a slide. The text is twice
the default size (`base_size = 22`). The title states the finding,
with the slope rounded. `geom_smooth(method = "lm")` draws the fitted
line. `label_dollar(accuracy = 1)`, from the package `scales`
(installed with the tidyverse), writes the axis numbers as whole
dollars. The colors and
their legend are gone, because the pitch does not discuss the regions.
The chunk draws the figure at the shape of a slide, 10 by 5.625
inches.

```{r slide-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.625, out.width = "100%"}
# slide_figure <- ggplot(countries, aes(x = gdp, y = life)) +
#   geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
#   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.5) +
#   scale_x_log10(breaks = c(300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000),
#                 labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
#   labs(title = "Ten times the income goes with 10 more years",
#        x = "GDP per person (log scale)",
#        y = "Life expectancy (years)") +
#   theme_minimal(base_size = 22)
# slide_figure
```

## Your figure for a slide

Please choose the figure from your report that carries your key
finding, and copy its code into the chunk below in place of the
skeleton. The skeleton is a scatterplot; if your figure is of another
kind (a bar chart, a box plot, a faceted figure), please start from
your report's own code instead. If your report changed the data before
drawing the figure (with `na_if()` or `factor()`, for instance),
please copy those lines in too. Then make the changes from the
handout's "A figure for a slide". `my_figure` is your figure.

```{r my-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.625, out.width = "100%"}
# my_data <- read_csv("data/YOUR-FILE.csv")
# my_figure <- ggplot(my_data, aes(x = PREDICTOR, y = OUTCOME)) +
#   geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
#   labs(title = "THE FINDING IN A FEW WORDS",
#        x = "PREDICTOR IN WORDS (UNITS)",
#        y = "OUTCOME IN WORDS (UNITS)") +
#   theme_minimal(base_size = 22)
# my_figure
```

`ggsave()` writes `my_figure` to `pitch-figure.png`, beside this
sheet, at the shape of a slide, ready to put on one.

```{r save-figure}
# ggsave("pitch-figure.png", my_figure, width = 10, height = 5.625,
#        dpi = 200)
```
